examples.en: A female flight attendant handed out drinks on the plane.

examples.ko: 여승무원은 안전 교육을 꼭 받아야 해요.
examples.en: Female crew members must receive safety training.
My friend passed the exam to become a flight attendant.
The female crew members greeted us with smiles.
I asked the female train attendant for directions.
When I was little, my dream was to be a flight attendant.

explain: 비행기나 열차에서 일하는 여성 승무원을 가리키지만, 성별을 따로 밝힐 필요가 없으면 그냥 '승무원'이라고 해도 돼요. 같은 틀로 '남승무원'도 있어요.

phrases.en: My older sister works as a female flight attendant for an airline.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비행기에서 일하는 여성 승무원을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a woman who works aboard an airplane.

phrases.en: There was also a male crew member on this flight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 틀로 만든 말로, 남자 승무원을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Built the same way, referring to a male crew member.

phrases.en: The crew member checked the seat belts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성별을 밝힐 필요가 없을 때 쓰는 더 일반적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more general term when gender doesn't need to be mentioned.

explain_en: It refers to a woman working as crew on a plane or train, but if you don't need to mention gender, simply saying '승무원' is fine. The same pattern gives '남승무원' for men.

examples.en: If you lose your passport, ask the consul for help.
A consul protects citizens of their own country who live abroad.
You have to make a reservation first to meet the consul.

examples.ko: 새로 온 영사가 교민 모임에 참석했어요.
examples.en: The newly arrived consul attended a meeting of overseas Koreans.
I got home safely with the consul's help.

examples.ko: 그 대사관에서 일하는 영사와 인사를 나눴어요.
examples.en: I greeted the consul who works at that embassy.

explain: 대사는 나라를 대표해 정치적인 일을 하고, 영사는 여권이나 비자처럼 국민과 직접 관련된 일을 맡아요. 일하는 곳도 보통 대사는 대사관, 영사는 영사관이에요. 가장 높은 영사는 '총영사'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I went to the consulate and applied for a visa.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영사가 일하는 곳으로, 여권이나 비자 일을 하러 갈 때 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The place where a consul works, often mentioned for passport or visa matters.

phrases.en: The consul general attended the event for overseas Koreans.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영사 중에서 가장 높은 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The title for the highest-ranking consul.

phrases.en: Reissuing a passport falls under consular work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외국에 사는 자국민을 돕는 일을 가리킬 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the work of helping one's citizens who live abroad.

explain_en: An 대사 represents the country and handles political matters, while a 영사 deals with things directly tied to citizens, such as passports and visas. Usually an 대사 works at an 대사관 and a 영사 at an 영사관. The highest-ranking consul is called a 총영사.

examples.en: The teaching assistant handed out the class materials.
If you have a question, ask the teaching assistant.
My older brother works as a teaching assistant in graduate school.
Thanks to the teaching assistant, I finished my homework well.
A teaching assistant helps the professor with work.
They say the lab is hiring a new teaching assistant.

explain: 대학이나 학원에서 교수님이나 강사를 도와주는 사람이에요. 직접 부를 때는 '조교님'이라고 해요. 선생님과 달리 수업을 맡기보다 자료 준비, 채점, 질문 응답을 돕는 보조 역할이 중심이에요.

phrases.en: Teaching assistant, when is this homework due?
phrases.nuance_ko: 조교를 직접 부르거나 말할 때 존경을 담아 붙이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The respectful form used when addressing or referring to a TA directly.

phrases.en: I work as a teaching assistant at a university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업이나 역할을 말할 때 '~로 일하다'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '~로 일하다' to talk about a job or role.

phrases.en: The class TA helps with grading.
phrases.nuance_ko: 특정 수업을 돕는 조교를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a TA who assists with a specific class.

explain_en: Assists a professor or class; in the military, a training instructor. A person who assists the professor or instructor at a university or academy. You address them as '조교님'. Unlike a teacher, they mostly support with materials, grading, and answering questions rather than leading the class.

examples.en: The principal will retire at the end of this year.
The president stepped down after working for a long time.
The president left office and returned to the hometown.
On the day of the retirement, the staff gave a bouquet.

examples.ko: 그 의사는 병원에서 퇴임한 후에도 봉사를 해요.
examples.en: That doctor still volunteers after leaving the hospital post.

examples.ko: 내년에 퇴임할 예정이라서 요즘 정리하고 있어요.
examples.en: I plan to step down next year, so I am sorting things out these days.

explain: 일반 직원이 회사를 그만둘 때는 '퇴직하다'나 '그만두다'를 쓰고, '퇴임하다'는 사장, 교장, 대통령처럼 맡은 자리에서 물러날 때 써요. 반대말은 '취임하다'예요. 정년이 되어 일을 마치는 건 '정년퇴직하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Tomorrow is the principal's retirement ceremony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자리에서 물러날 때 하는 행사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the ceremony held when someone leaves a post.

phrases.en: After retiring, I want to live in my hometown.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자리에서 물러난 뒤의 시간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the time after leaving a post.

phrases.en: The president is going to retire next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 물러날 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about a planned future retirement.

explain_en: Formal, for principals, professors or officials leaving a post. For ordinary employees leaving a company, use 퇴직하다 or 그만두다. 퇴임하다 is for stepping down from a post held by someone like a president, principal or head of state. The opposite is 취임하다. Finishing work at retirement age is 정년퇴직하다.

t90.ax: The principal will retire at the end of this year.

examples.en: The editorial department reread the article and fixed it.
I work in the editorial department of a magazine company.

examples.ko: 편집부 직원들이 마감 때문에 밤을 새웠어요.
examples.en: The editorial staff stayed up all night because of the deadline.
You can send the manuscript to the editorial department.
A newspaper's editorial department also decides the headlines.

examples.ko: 편집부 회의가 오후 세 시에 열려요.
examples.en: The editorial meeting is held at three in the afternoon.

explain: 편집부는 신문사, 출판사, 잡지사에서 글을 고치고 지면을 짜는 부서예요. 취재하는 곳은 '취재부', 광고를 파는 곳은 '광고부'처럼 부서 이름에 '부'를 붙여요. 한 사람은 '편집자'나 '에디터'라고 불러요.

phrases.example: 편집부 직원이 제 글을 읽어 줬어요.
phrases.en: An editorial department staff member read my writing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부서에서 일하는 사람을 말할 때 뒤에 '직원'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 직원 to refer to someone working in the department.

phrases.en: There is an editorial department meeting this afternoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부서 안에서 하는 회의를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to a meeting held within the department.

phrases.en: I'm an editor who makes books.
phrases.nuance_ko: '편집부'는 부서이고, '편집자'는 그곳에서 일하는 한 사람이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 편집부 is the department, while 편집자 is one person who works there.

explain_en: 편집부 is the department at a newspaper, publisher or magazine that edits text and lays out pages. Department names take 부, as in 취재부 (reporting) and 광고부 (advertising). One person there is a 편집자 or an 에디터.

examples.en: The dean of our college is very kind.
The dean gave a congratulatory speech at the graduation ceremony.
A new person has come as dean of the art college.
I asked the dean about scholarships.
I made an appointment for a meeting with the dean.

examples.ko: 그분은 학장이 되기 전에 오랫동안 교수였어요.
examples.en: Before becoming dean, that person was a professor for many years.

explain: '총장'은 대학 전체의 우두머리이고, '학장'은 공과대학·인문대학 같은 단과대학의 우두머리예요. 직접 부를 때는 '학장님'이라고 해요. 고등학교의 우두머리는 '학장'이 아니라 '교장'이에요.

phrases.en: I greeted the dean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 부르거나 높여 말할 때는 '님'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 님 when addressing or referring to the dean respectfully.

phrases.en: I had a meeting in the dean's office.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학장이 일하는 방을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the room where the dean works.

phrases.en: A new dean of the engineering college has arrived.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어느 단과대학인지 앞에 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the name of the college in front to say which one.

explain_en: A 총장 heads the whole university, while a 학장 heads one college inside it, such as engineering or humanities. When addressing the person directly, say 학장님. The head of a high school is a 교장, not a 학장.

examples.en: They say arrogance makes people fail.

examples.ko: 성공한 뒤에 교만에 빠지는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people fall into arrogance after they succeed.

examples.ko: 그의 교만 때문에 팀 분위기가 나빠졌어요.
examples.en: His arrogance made the team atmosphere worse.

examples.ko: 교만을 버리고 다른 사람의 말을 들어 보세요.
examples.en: Put aside your arrogance and listen to what others say.
If arrogance goes too far, it's easy to lose friends.
Adults say humility is better than arrogance.

explain: 반대말은 '겸손'이에요. '거만'은 겉으로 드러나는 건방진 태도에, '자만'은 자기를 대단하게 여기는 마음에 더 가까워요. 교만은 글이나 교훈 같은 말에서 자주 만나요.

phrases.en: Give up your arrogance and learn humbly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교훈 같은 말에서 반대말 '겸손'과 함께 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in moral advice alongside its opposite, 겸손.

phrases.en: When you become arrogant, it's easy to make mistakes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교만을 마음의 상태로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Talks about arrogance as a state of mind.

phrases.en: I lost a friend because of my arrogance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교만이 나쁜 결과의 원인임을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say arrogance is the cause of a bad result.

explain_en: Formal, moral/religious — excessive pride as a character flaw. Its opposite is '겸손' (humility). '거만' leans toward an outwardly rude, haughty attitude, and '자만' toward thinking too highly of yourself. '교만' is often met in writing and moral sayings.

t90.ax: They say arrogance makes people fail.

examples.ko: 의대를 졸업한 뒤 군의관으로 군 복무를 하는 사람들이 있어요.
examples.en: Some people finish medical school and then do their military service as army doctors.

examples.ko: 군의관이 훈련 중 다친 병사를 치료해 줬어요.
examples.en: The army doctor treated the soldier who was hurt during training.

examples.ko: 삼촌은 군대에서 군의관을 도와 환자를 돌봤어요.
examples.en: My uncle helped the army doctor take care of patients in the military.

examples.ko: 몸이 너무 아파서 군의관에게 진료를 받았어요.
examples.en: I was so sick that I got examined by the army doctor.

examples.ko: 군의관님이 퇴원해도 된다고 하셔서 집에 갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: The army doctor said I could be discharged, so I can go home.

examples.ko: 아버지는 군의관 출신이라 응급 처치를 잘 아세요.
examples.en: My father used to be an army doctor, so he knows first aid well.

explain: 군대 안에서 병사들을 진료하는 의사를 부르는 말이고, 직접 부를 때는 '군의관님'이라고 해요. 치료를 돕는 병사인 '의무병'과 달리 군의관은 의사예요. 군대 이야기를 할 때 자주 나오는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 군의관님, 어제부터 열이 나고 머리가 아파요.
phrases.en: Doctor, I've had a fever and a headache since yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군의관을 직접 부를 때는 이름 대신 '군의관님'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is how you address an army doctor directly, instead of using a name.

phrases.en: My uncle is serving as an army doctor now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대에서 의사로 일하는 것을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for working as a doctor in the military.
phrases.en_equiv: to serve as an army surgeon

phrases.example: 다친 병사는 바로 군 병원으로 옮겨졌어요.
phrases.en: The injured soldier was moved to a military hospital right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군의관이 일하는 곳이에요. 군인을 치료하는 병원을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The place where army doctors work, a hospital that treats soldiers.

explain_en: It names the doctor who treats soldiers inside the military, and when addressing one directly you say '군의관님'. Unlike a '의무병' (a medic soldier who assists in treatment), a 군의관 is a physician. It comes up often when people talk about military life.

examples.en: During college, I stayed at my uncle's house.
Grandfather lives alone in a small room.
He lived at a temple while writing the book.
The dormitory where the international students live is next to the school.
I haven't decided yet where to stay.
Would it be okay if I stayed at your place for a while?

explain: '살다'나 '지내다'보다 글 같고 점잖은 말이에요. 어디에 머물며 생활하는지를 말할 때 써서, 임시로 머무는 집이나 절, 기숙사 같은 곳에 잘 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '살다', '지내다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 여행 중에 작은 절에서 며칠 기거했어요.
phrases.en: During my trip, I stayed at a small temple for a few days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거 해요체로, 어딘가에 머물며 지냈다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past polite form meaning one stayed and lived somewhere.

phrases.en: I live together with my grandmother in the same house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람과 같은 곳에서 생활할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when living in the same place with someone else.

phrases.example: 학생들이 기거하는 곳은 학교 근처 기숙사예요.
phrases.en: The place where the students live is a dorm near the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 머물며 지내는 장소를 점잖게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A dignified way to refer to the place where someone lives.

explain_en: It is more formal and written than '살다' or '지내다'. It is used for where someone stays and lives, fitting temporary places like a relative's house, temple or dorm. In daily conversation, people usually say '살다' or '지내다'.

t90.ax: I haven't decided yet where to stay.

examples.ko: 설날에 할아버지는 한복 위에 두루마기를 입으셨어요.
examples.en: On New Year's Day, Grandpa wore a durumagi over his hanbok.
In winter a durumagi is warm, so people wear it like a coat.
I wore a durumagi to the wedding.
The durumagi sleeves were long, so I rolled them up.

examples.ko: 아버지가 새 두루마기를 맞추러 한복집에 가셨어요.
examples.en: My father went to the hanbok shop to have a new durumagi made.
I saw a Joseon-era durumagi at the museum.

explain: 한복 위에 입는 겉옷으로, 외투처럼 입는 옷이에요. 화장실에서 쓰는 '두루마리 휴지'의 '두루마리'(둘둘 만 것)와 소리가 비슷하니 헷갈리지 마세요.

phrases.en: On the holiday I wore a durumagi and bowed to my elders.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 입을 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for putting on the garment.

phrases.en: I came home and took off my durumagi.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉옷이라서 집에 들어오면 벗는 모습이 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: As an outer coat, it is natural to take it off indoors.

phrases.en: I had a new hanbok durumagi made.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한복과 함께 쓰는 겉옷임을 분명히 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes clear it is an outer coat worn with hanbok.

explain_en: It is an outer garment worn over hanbok, like an overcoat. Don't confuse it with '두루마리' (something rolled up), as in '두루마리 휴지' (toilet paper roll), which sounds similar.

examples.en: There is a formal dinner at the embassy tonight.
The two countries' representatives shared a banquet.
Korean food was served on the banquet menu.
We held a small formal dinner with just family.

examples.ko: 결혼 전날에 친구들이 만찬을 준비해 줬어요.
examples.en: The day before the wedding, my friends prepared a feast for me.

examples.ko: 그 만찬에는 옷을 차려입고 가야 해요.
examples.en: You have to dress up for that dinner.

explain: 특별한 손님이나 행사를 위해 차린 격식 있는 저녁 식사를 말해요. 평소 저녁밥은 '저녁'이나 '저녁 식사'라고 해요. 뉴스에서 정상 회담 뒤의 '공식 만찬'으로 아주 자주 나오고, 집에서 일상적으로 쓰는 말은 아니에요.

phrases.example: 정상 회담 뒤에 공식 만찬이 열렸어요.
phrases.en: An official banquet was held after the summit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in the news.

phrases.en: The president invited the delegation to a banquet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 격식 있는 자리에 손님을 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for inviting guests to a formal dinner.

phrases.example: 오늘 저녁 식사는 가족과 함께 했어요.
phrases.en: I had dinner with my family today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 평소에 먹는 저녁은 '만찬'이 아니라 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: For an ordinary evening meal, say this instead of 만찬.

explain_en: Formal or lavish dinner, often for guests or events. A formal evening meal laid out for special guests or events. A normal dinner is 저녁 or 저녁 식사. In news it appears constantly as 공식 만찬 after summits, and it is not an everyday home word.

t90.ax: You have to dress up for that dinner.

en: moment of bewilderment; moment of confusion

examples.en: Before I knew it, I had answered 'yes'.

examples.ko: 얼떨결에 친구 대신 발표를 맡게 됐어요.
examples.en: I ended up giving the presentation for my friend before I knew what was happening.
I said it without thinking, but I also meant it.
While answering the phone, I blurted out my password in confusion.

examples.ko: 얼떨결에 시작한 운동이 이제는 취미가 됐어요.
examples.en: The exercise I started without really thinking has now become a hobby.

examples.ko: 얼떨결에 받은 명함을 지갑에 넣어 두었어요.
examples.en: I put the business card I took in the confusion of the moment into my wallet.

explain: 거의 '얼떨결에' 꼴로 쓰고, 정신이 없거나 당황한 사이에 생각 없이 하게 된 행동을 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '엉겁결에'가 있어요. 결과가 좋든 나쁘든 쓸 수 있고, 나중에 '얼떨결에 했는데 잘됐어요'처럼 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: Before I knew it, I had raised my hand.
phrases.nuance_ko: '얼떨결에'와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 둘 다 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning as 얼떨결에, and both are common.
phrases.en_equiv: in the heat of the moment

phrases.example: 얼떨결에 친구를 따라갔다가 좋은 사람을 만났어요.
phrases.en: I followed my friend without thinking and met a nice person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각할 틈 없이 따라간 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes following someone without time to think.

phrases.en: I promised in a flustered moment that I would go out on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 당황해서 하게 된 약속에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a promise made in a flustered moment.

explain_en: It is almost always used as '얼떨결에', for something done without thinking because you were flustered or in a rush. A similar word is '엉겁결에'. It works whether the result is good or bad, for example '얼떨결에 했는데 잘됐어요' (I did it on impulse and it turned out well).

examples.ko: 할아버지는 매일 아침 일찍 진지를 자셔요.
examples.en: Grandfather eats his meal early every morning.
Mother is having lunch right now.
What did the teacher eat yesterday evening?
The food that the elderly person eats needs to be soft.

examples.ko: 약을 자시려면 먼저 식사를 하셔야 해요.
examples.en: If you are going to take the medicine, you need to eat a meal first.
Won't it be too spicy for the elder to eat?

explain: '먹다'의 높임말로 '드시다', '잡수시다'와 같은 뜻이에요. 요즘 일상에서는 '드세요'가 훨씬 자연스럽고, '자시다'는 어르신께 쓰는 옛스러운 말투로 들려요. 이미 높임말이라 자기 자신에게는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: Grandmother, please have this fruit.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자시다'와 같은 높임말인데 요즘 일상에서 훨씬 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same honorific as 자시다, but much more natural in daily speech today.

phrases.en: Grandfather is having dinner.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자시다'처럼 어르신께 쓰는 높임말이고 조금 격식 있게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: An honorific for elders like 자시다, with a slightly more formal feel.

phrases.en: The side dishes my father eats are always the same.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자시다'가 뒤의 명사를 꾸며 주는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A conjugated form where 자시다 modifies the noun that follows.

explain_en: It is the honorific of '먹다' and has the same meaning as '드시다' and '잡수시다'. In daily life these days '드세요' is much more natural, and '자시다' sounds old-fashioned, used toward elders. Since it is already honorific, you never use it for yourself.

t90.ax: Mother is having lunch right now.

examples.ko: 아버지 칠순 잔치를 가족끼리 하기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to hold my father's 70th birthday party with just family.
My grandmother, who has turned seventy, is still healthy.
We sent them on a trip to celebrate their 70th birthday.
My aunt had photos taken for her 70th birthday.
A teacher who is past seventy came to give a lecture.
What would be good to give as a 70th birthday gift?

explain: 일흔 살을 가리키는 말로, 주로 부모님이나 어르신의 생신을 말할 때 써요. 60세는 '환갑', 80세는 '팔순'이라고 해요. 어르신께는 '칠순이세요'처럼 높여 말해요.

phrases.en: My grandfather turned seventy this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일흔 살 생신이 되었다는 뜻이에요. 어르신께는 '맞으시다'로 높여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means reaching the seventieth birthday; use '맞으시다' to show respect.

phrases.en: My mother is seventy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어르신의 나이를 높여서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A respectful way to state an elder's age.

phrases.example: 부모님 칠순 선물로 여행을 보내 드렸어요.
phrases.en: I sent my parents on a trip as a seventieth birthday gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 칠순 때 드리는 선물을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a gift given on someone's seventieth birthday.

explain_en: It refers to the age of seventy and is mainly used for the birthdays of parents and elders. Sixty is '환갑' and eighty is '팔순'. For an elder you say it politely, as in '칠순이세요'.

examples.en: The retainer said to the emperor, 'Your Majesty, I beg to report.'

examples.ko: 사극에서 폐하라고 부르는 장면을 많이 봐요.
examples.en: I often see scenes in period dramas where they call the emperor 'Your Majesty'.
The retainer announced that His Majesty the Emperor had arrived.
The general set out after receiving the Emperor's order.

examples.ko: 영화 속 왕비는 폐하를 몹시 걱정했어요.
examples.en: In the movie, the queen worried about the Emperor deeply.

examples.ko: 폐하 앞에서는 고개를 들 수 없었어요.
examples.en: In front of the Emperor, no one could lift their head.

explain: 역사극에서 황제에게는 '폐하', 조선의 왕에게는 '전하'라고 불러요. 지금은 사극이나 외국 왕실 이야기에서만 들을 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The ministers bowed to His Majesty the Emperor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '황제'와 같이 써서 높이는 사람이 누구인지 분명히 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with 황제 to make clear whom is being honored.

phrases.en: His Majesty summoned his ministers today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주어를 높이는 '께서'를 붙여 쓰는 꼴이에요. 사극에서 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific subject particle 께서 is attached. Often heard in historical dramas.

phrases.en: The minister followed His Majesty's command.
phrases.nuance_ko: '폐하의 ~' 꼴로 황제의 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The 폐하의 ~ pattern is used for things belonging to the emperor.

explain_en: In historical dramas an emperor is addressed as '폐하', while a Joseon king is addressed as '전하'. Today you hear it only in period dramas or stories about foreign royal families.
